text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper presents an original integrated modeling study focused on simulating future land use/land cover (LULC) changes across the entire country of China—a national-scale spatial implementation. Its primary objective is to project and compare LULC dynamics under two distinct future scenarios (Scenario A: increasing grain yield; Scenario B: constant yield). The methodology explicitly couples socioeconomic, ecological, and spatial allocation models to produce quantitative, spatially explicit LULC projections for 2020, 2050, and 2080. The results include mapped outputs (Figures 6–8), quantitative change rates (e.g., cropland decreases by 27.37% in Scenario A vs. increases by 29.41% in Scenario B by 2080), and a conversion matrix derived from historical data with validation against observed land use (Figure 3). All core inclusion criteria are met: national scale, primary focus on LULC prediction, ≥2 future scenarios with quantitative comparison, spatially explicit modeling, and mapped projections. None of the exclusion criteria apply.)
